title: Joomla planner: one unreadable batch keeps its words and the rest are written; icon markup never reaches the model
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/cms/tracy-seeder/test/plan-joomla-contract.test.mjs

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the results of the cases whose names start with "🔒 a batch the model never answers readably" and "markup with no words in it never reaches the model".

S3: Run: node --input-type=module -e "import { isMarkupOnly } from './packages/cms/tracy-seeder/src/plan-joomla-contract.mjs'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; const m = JSON.parse(readFileSync('packages/cms/tracy-joomla-quickstart/contracts/ja-vega/j6/1.0.3/content-map.json','utf8')); const svg = m.slots.filter(s => /\(\(\s*svg/i.test(String(s.sample||''))); console.log(svg.length, svg.filter(s => isMarkupOnly(s.sample)).length)" and record the output.
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 18).

Both named cases are 'ok': a batch whose answer is cut off keeps its slots pending as 'model-unreadable' while the other batch is written; nothing readable at all still rejects with 'Content mapping refused 3 times'; a thrown model call still reaches the caller; an icon sample is neither asked about nor pending.
S3 prints '11 11': every SVG icon text slot of ja-vega/j6/1.0.3 is recognised as markup with no words.
evidence: 05/10/2026 local stand: Apply on Design inspiration ja-vega (Joomla) failed in 1 of 2 runs, 'Content mapping refused 3 times: ... not valid JSON', nothing written. Replaying that contract's plan with the real model: the same 33-slot batch was cut off 3/3 times in the middle of SVG path data (11 text slots hold ((svg ...)) icons up to 3.2 kB). After the fix: 3/3 Apply runs applied (397, 349 slots).
fence: Markup-only samples are left as the template made them; a batch with no readable answer after the retries is pending and the plan goes on; a plan with no readable batch, or a model that throws, still fails loudly.
